transcript.content: Hello, and welcome. I'm Dr. [Name], a psychiatrist. What brings you in to see me today?

Hi, Doctor. Thank you so much for taking the time to see me, I really appreciate it. 

Um, well, I hope I'm explaining this right, but... what made me come in is that, for the past year or so, I've just been noticing this little habit I have. It's probably nothing major, I mean, I'm the chief executive at my company so I still get things done, but the smallest things seem to pull me off what I’m doing before I can even stop it. Like, just a phone buzz, or somebody walking past my office door, or... honestly, even just a random thought popping into my head about my in-laws. It just completely shifts my focus. 

I try really hard to keep it together, and I know everyone gets sidetracked sometimes, but I just wanted to make sure I'm doing everything right to stay on top of things. Does that make sense? Is that the sort of thing you can help with?
Over this past year, have you noticed any changes in your mood—like feeling more anxious, worried, sad, or unusually energetic or irritable—alongside these attention difficulties?

Um, no, actually. Thankfully, no. I mean, I try to stay pretty positive overall. I definitely haven't felt sad or, you know, overly anxious. 

Obviously, running a business has its normal day-to-day stresses, but I wouldn't say I'm unusually worried or irritable or anything like that. I always try to keep a really good attitude for my team, so I make sure not to let things get to me. So, yeah, my mood has been totally fine, I think. 

I hope that's a good sign? I just want to make sure I'm giving you the right information.
When you think back to your childhood and school years, do you remember having similar difficulties with attention and focus, or is this something that's really new over just this past year?

Um, well, that's a really good question. I guess... if I'm being completely honest—and I really want to make sure I'm giving you the full picture here—it's not entirely new. Looking back, this sort of thing was around when I was a kid, too. 

I was just a really enthusiastic boy, you know? But, um, my teachers were always moving my seat around in class. I guess I talked a bit too much, or sometimes I'd just get up without asking first. And I had this habit where I'd just sort of... blurt things out before they even finished asking the question. 

I really wasn't trying to be disruptive or anything, I promise. I just got so eager to participate and my mind would just go a mile a minute. I hope that doesn't make me sound like I was a terrible student? I just want to make sure I'm answering your question the way you need me to.
From your teenage years through to now as an adult, would you say you've always had these kinds of attention and focus difficulties, or were there times when they got better or went away for a while?

Well, um... I guess for a long time, I just sort of channeled all that extra energy into my work, you know? Building the business and everything. So it wasn't really a problem for most of my adult life. I've always been a little on the go, but I made it work. 

But, um... if I'm looking at when it really became an issue again... it's been noticeably harder to manage for about a year and two months now. That's, well, that's right around the time some... some conflict with my in-laws started taking over more of our family life. 

I try really hard not to let personal things affect my day-to-day, I really do, but I guess that added stress just made it a bit tougher to keep my focus as sharp as usual. I hope that answers what you were asking? I just want to make sure I'm giving you the timeline you need.

If the conflict with your in-laws were to resolve tomorrow, do you think your ability to focus and concentrate would return to how it was before that stress started, or do you think you'd still struggle with distractions the same way?

Um, wow, that's... that's a really good question. I guess I haven't really thought about it exactly like that. 

If all that stress just disappeared tomorrow... well, I mean, I'd like to think things would go right back to normal. I really would. I try to be the kind of person who bounces back, you know? But... um, honestly? I'm not entirely sure. 

Even before all this family stuff, I've always been a little bit... well, you know, restless. Always needing to be doing something, always moving. So maybe I'd still have a little bit of trouble sitting still or keeping perfectly focused on one thing for too long. I mean, I really hope I'd be better! I'd certainly try my hardest to be. 

But, um, I guess I can't say for absolute certain that it would all just magically go away. Does that make sense? I hope that's a helpful answer, I'm just trying to be as realistic as possible for you.

When you were managing your business successfully over those years before the family conflict started—say, five years ago or more—how much were you actually struggling with distractions and focus back then, or were those symptoms pretty much under control?

Um, well, back then... I'd say things were actually pretty good. I mean, I was really focused on building everything up, so I was always on the go. 

I guess, you know, I might have had a little trouble sitting through really long meetings, or maybe I'd jump from one project to another pretty quickly. But I always made sure the work got done! I really prided myself on that. I just sort of used that energy to keep the momentum going, if that makes sense? 

So, um, I wouldn't say I was really struggling with distractions back then. It was more like... I was just a really hands-on, energetic boss. I hope that's the kind of information you're looking for? I just want to make sure I'm giving you an accurate picture of how things used to be.

Before the family conflict started about a year ago, if you think back to your work as CEO—did you ever feel like your attention problems were actually causing you real trouble, or did the structure of running your own business just naturally fit with how your mind works?

Well, um... before the family stuff, I'd say the business really did just kind of fit how I operate. Being the boss meant I could bounce around, and people just saw it as me being driven, you know? But... um... lately, with the way things are now... 

I mean, I'm still keeping up overall! The business is fine, I promise I'm not letting everything fall apart. But... I guess I have noticed that it's starting to cost me a little bit. Like, um, at home, my wife gets frustrated when I zone out during family plans, and I can tell I'm losing a bit of trust there. And at work, when I'm mentoring someone or we're in a meeting and I keep fidgeting or interrupting... I can see people losing their patience with me. 

I try so hard to be present for them, I really do. It's just... things don't always go the way they should right now. I hope that makes sense? I just want to be totally honest with you, even if it's a little embarrassing to admit I'm frustrating the people I care about. Am I giving you the right kind of details?

When you compare how you're struggling with focus right now to how you were as a child in school—with the blurting out and the restlessness—are the problems you're having today actually worse or different in some way, or are they pretty much the same kind of thing you've always dealt with?

Um, well... that's an interesting way to look at it. I guess, if I really think about it... it's probably the same kind of thing I've always dealt with. 

I mean, looking back—and I hope this is okay to say, I was just a kid and kids have a lot of energy, right?—but back in school, teachers were always, um, moving my seat. They said I talked too much, or I'd get up without asking, or... well, I guess I had a bad habit of blurting things out before they even finished asking the question. 

I really didn't mean to be disruptive! I just got so eager to participate, you know? But yeah, I suppose the restlessness I'm feeling now is... well, it's pretty similar to how I was back then. Just, you know, adult versions of it. I hope that answers your question? I'm just trying to give you the most accurate picture I can.
